title: Uncertainty Disentanglement for Multimodal Foundation Models in Robotic Systems
problem: Multimodal foundation models used in robotic systems conflate perception uncertainty (sensor/input noise) and decision uncertainty (model ambiguity), making it impossible to reason about or mitigate each type independently.
motivation: Reliable autonomous systems require knowing whether failures stem from bad sensor input or from inherent model uncertainty, enabling targeted interventions such as active sensing or model refinement.
method: Conformal prediction quantifies perception uncertainty by constructing calibrated prediction sets for multimodal inputs. Decision uncertainty is modeled via Formally-specified Markov Decision Processes (FMDP) using Kripke structures and temporal logic specifications, enabling formal verification of behavioral compliance. Active sensing triggers additional observations when perception uncertainty is high; automated model refinement is triggered when decision uncertainty is high. Evaluated on LLaVA-1.5-7B and CLIP on the Carla simulator and real-world driving data.
key_novelty: First framework to formally disentangle perception uncertainty (conformal prediction) from decision uncertainty (FMDP + temporal logic) in multimodal robotic systems, enabling targeted mitigation strategies for each uncertainty type.
contributions: Formal taxonomy distinguishing perception uncertainty from decision uncertainty in multimodal robotic systems
Conformal prediction-based perception uncertainty quantification with statistical guarantees
FMDP formulation using Kripke structures and temporal logic for decision uncertainty
Active sensing strategy triggered by perception uncertainty
Automated model refinement strategy triggered by decision uncertainty
Evaluation on LLaVA-1.5-7B + CLIP in Carla simulator and real-world driving

metrics.accuracy: 40% reduction in output variability; 5% improvement in specification satisfaction; 95%+ temporal logic compliance

baselines: Standard conformal prediction without decision modeling
limitations: FMDP formulation requires expert-specified temporal logic properties
Computational overhead of formal verification may limit real-time applicability
Evaluation limited to driving domain; generalization to other robotics tasks unverified
Conformal prediction requires calibration data from target distribution
